text:
anya: Heads-up — after merging slimpatch (PR #4821) last night my canary shows a consistent +12-18% host CPU on streaming requests. Spike's during parse/assemble of stream chunks, not GPU. https://perf.redwood/dashboard/ingress?run=1722
matt: ugh. any flamegraphs or pprof heap/CPU? which binary? host-proxy or preparse sidecar?
jordan: sounds like parse fragmentation -> kvcache churn. did slimpatch change header-coalesce timing?
anya: it's the host-preparse binary. pprof snapshot: `go tool pprof -web host-preparse.cpu.001.pb.gz` — biggest stacks point to parse_token_frame->assemble_chunk->kv_cache_lookup
sam: can you paste a small pprof snippet or top5 funcs?
anya: sure — paste:
``
25.4%  parse_token_frame
18.1%  assemble_chunk
12.7%  kv_cache_evict
9.3%   http2_read_frame
5.0%   net_read
```
lee: kv_cache_evict at 12.7% is worrying. we recently tightened max_fragment_age in slimpatch, might be causing more small fragments and eviction thrash.
matt: also check kernel-selection logs — if sequence lengths are shorter due to aggressive chunking, runtime may pick smaller kernels frequently which increases CPU overhead.
jordan: yep. when kernel selection toggles per-request it adds overhead. we should log kernel variant selection counts for a minute and see.
anya: I grepped kvcache evict counts from tonight's run:
``
[2026-03-20T02:12:01Z] evict_count=4829 path=/ingress/host-preparse shard=17
[2026-03-20T02:12:31Z] evict_count=5170 path=/ingress/host-preparse shard=17
[2026-03-20T02:13:01Z] evict_count=6032 path=/ingress/host-preparse shard=17
```
sam: that looks like rapid growth. we should check per-shard KV hit rates too. if cache working set shrinks due to fragmentation, latency/cpu go up.
lee: suggestion: bump the fragment coalesce threshold back up by 2x and increase kvcache.shard_size to reduce eviction frequency. also consider a small LRU hold-time.
matt: alternative: delay kernel selection until after prefix is parsed so we compute kernel once per session not per fragment — cheap memoization.
jordan: +1 for memoization. also adjust batching heuristics: increase batch_max_delay_ms to 4ms for streaming clients to let small fragments coalesce.
anya: quick mitigation: rolling back the slimpatch is easy but i'd prefer a targeted tweak: restore old max_fragment_age and enable kernel selection memoization.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollback-slimpatch -> env=canary user=anya ticket=INF-2219
anya: thanks — I'll monitor CPU and kvcache evict rates. if that doesn't drop we'll revert fully.
sam: put an observability task to surface per-request kernel decisions and per-session kvcache hit-rate in console (small dashboard)
lee: I'll open a small PR for kvcache default shard_size bump and fragment threshold revert.
matt: assigning follow-ups: lee -> PR for kvcache; jordan -> kernel memoization patch; sam -> dashboard. check in 30m.
anya: sounds good. :thumbsup:
